chunks: Rifāʿah ibn Mūsā asked Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام:
about a person who is dyed, if he is able to perform sajdah and recitation, whether he may pray while in his dye.
He said: "Yes, if his cloth is taharah and he is in wudu (ablution). And there is no harm in a woman praying while she is dyed and her hands are bound."

key_terms.الْمُخْتَضِبِ: a person who has applied dye, such as henna
key_terms.خِرْقَتُهُ: his cloth or rag used in the dyeing process
key_terms.مُتَوَضِّئًا: being in a state of wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Can a person pray while wearing dye such as henna if they are able to perform sajdah and are in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that praying while one is in the state of applying dye is permissible, provided the person can perform the required acts of salat and maintains ritual purity. It also states that a woman may pray while dyed and with her hands bound, indicating that such circumstances do not invalidate the prayer when its essential conditions are met.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.824 - Rifa'ah ibn Musa asked Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)
about a person who is dyed (with henna or similar) and whether they can pray while in this state if they are able to perform prostration and recitation.

Imam (as) replied: "Yes, as long as their cloth (used during the process) is pure and they are in a state of wudu (ritual purity). There is also no issue if a woman prays while She is dyed and her hands are bound (covered)."
